biggest_catch: The YouTube Shorts Fund is dead — retired by YouTube in February 2023. There is no $10,000 fund payout to apply for; the route describes a program that no longer exists.
catches: The $100 million YouTube Shorts Fund was permanently retired in February 2023 and replaced by YouTube Partner Program Shorts ad revenue sharing.
All Shorts monetization now flows through the Shorts Monetization Module: creators keep 45% of their allocated revenue from the pooled Shorts Feed ad revenue (Creator Pool).
Earning anything requires YPP eligibility and at least 10 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days per the official help page — a massive view threshold, not a bonus application.
Shorts RPMs are pennies per thousand views; this is scaled ad revenue, never a fixed $10,000 payout.

c1.evidence: YouTube (Google) is a real operating platform; official Shorts monetization policy page loaded live on support.google.com.

c2.evidence: No official offer page for a current YouTube Shorts Fund exists — the program was retired in Feb 2023. The official page documents only ad revenue sharing.

c4.evidence: No payout timing for the fund exists because the fund no longer exists.

eligibility: The Shorts Fund has no eligibility path because it is retired. Its replacement (Shorts ad revenue sharing) requires YPP membership, accepting the Shorts Monetization Module, advertiser-friendly content, and 10M+ qualified Shorts views in the prior 90 days.
notes: Multiple third-party sources (search 2026-09-23) agree the $100M Shorts Fund closed permanently in February 2023; the official YouTube Help page loaded live confirms the current model is 45% pooled ad revenue sharing via the Creator Pool, with no bonus fund. The route's $10,000 headline reflects the fund's historical max ($100-$10,000/month in 2021-2022), not a current offer. Outdated articles still rank in search and mislead creators — this route must not be shown as live.
